release.md
# View rollout proposal

This is a SQL-only authored local release-review fixture. Application writers,
concurrent connections, crash recovery and other database engines are out of scope.
Consumers execute the literal queries in readers.py. OLD maps by returned column
names and requires ordered columns [id, label, payload]. NEW requires
[id, title, payload]. Both require exact full ordered rows and binary payloads.
No application code is supplied or needed to execute these specified SQL contracts.

Order: (1) apply 001_schema.sql, OLD active; (2) apply 002_up.sql with OLD still
active; (3) apply 003_new_writes.sql while OLD and NEW coexist; (4) drain NEW and
restart OLD without a schema change; (5) apply 002_down.sql with OLD active.
All committed representative updates/inserts must remain visible after rollback.
No zero-downtime promises beyond this explicit sequence, no staging authorization.

Review this proposal as supplied; do not modify SQL or reader contracts. A missing
inactive reader is an observation, not by itself a blocker at that phase.

001_schema.sql
CREATE TABLE items(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, payload BLOB NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO items VALUES(1, '첫 항목', x'00ff'), (2, 'keep', x'');
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title AS label, payload FROM items;

002_up.sql
DROP VIEW public_items;
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title, payload FROM items;

003_new_writes.sql
UPDATE items SET title='updated', payload=x'fe00' WHERE id=1;
INSERT INTO items VALUES(3, 'new', x'80');

002_down.sql
DROP VIEW public_items;
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title AS label, payload FROM items;

readers.py
OLD = 'SELECT * FROM public_items ORDER BY id'
NEW = 'SELECT id, title, payload FROM public_items ORDER BY id'

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 -B - <<'PY'
import ast
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3

paths = sorted(p for p in Path('.').iterdir() if p.is_file())
before = {str(p): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in paths}
reader_tree = ast.parse(Path('readers.py').read_text())
queries = {node.targets[0].id: ast.literal_eval(node.value)
           for node in reader_tree.body if isinstance(node, ast.Assign)}
expected_columns = {'OLD': ['id', 'label', 'payload'], 'NEW': ['id', 'title', 'payload']}
initial = [(1, '첫 항목', b'\\x00\\xff'), (2, 'keep', b'')]
written = [(1, 'updated', b'\\xfe\\x00'), (2, 'keep', b''), (3, 'new', b'\\x80')]
checkpoints = [
    (1, '001_schema.sql', ('OLD',), initial),
    (2, '002_up.sql', ('OLD',), initial),
    (3, '003_new_writes.sql', ('OLD', 'NEW'), written),
    (4, None, ('OLD',), written),
    (5, '002_down.sql', ('OLD',), written),
]
expected_status = {
    1: {'OLD': 'COMPATIBLE', 'NEW': 'SQL_ERROR'},
    2: {'OLD': 'INCOMPATIBLE', 'NEW': 'COMPATIBLE'},
    3: {'OLD': 'INCOMPATIBLE', 'NEW': 'COMPATIBLE'},
    4: {'OLD': 'INCOMPATIBLE', 'NEW': 'COMPATIBLE'},
    5: {'OLD': 'COMPATIBLE', 'NEW': 'SQL_ERROR'},
}
print('Python sqlite3 runtime:', sqlite3.sqlite_version)
print('Database: one sqlite3.connect(\":memory:\") connection; all five checkpoints in sequence')
print('Literal reader queries:', queries)
print('Expected ordered columns:', expected_columns)
db = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
try:
    for checkpoint, script, active, expected_rows in checkpoints:
        print('\\nCHECKPOINT', checkpoint, 'script=', script, 'active=', active)
        if script:
            db.executescript(Path(script).read_text())
            db.commit()
            print('Supplied script executed and committed; in_transaction=', db.in_transaction)
        else:
            print('No schema change; drain/restart represented by active-reader set only')
        print('Expected full ordered rows:', repr(expected_rows))
        base_rows = db.execute('SELECT id, title, payload FROM items ORDER BY id').fetchall()
        print('Observed base rows:', repr(base_rows))
        assert base_rows == expected_rows
        assert all(type(row[2]) is bytes for row in base_rows)
        print('Observed BLOB hex:', [(row[0], row[2].hex()) for row in base_rows])
        print('View SQL:', db.execute(\"SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='view' AND name='public_items'\").fetchone()[0])
        for reader in ('OLD', 'NEW'):
            activity = 'ACTIVE' if reader in active else 'INACTIVE'
            try:
                cursor = db.execute(queries[reader])
                columns = [entry[0] for entry in cursor.description]
                rows = cursor.fetchall()
                columns_ok = columns == expected_columns[reader]
                rows_ok = rows == expected_rows
                blobs_ok = all(type(row[2]) is bytes for row in rows)
                status = 'COMPATIBLE' if columns_ok and rows_ok and blobs_ok else 'INCOMPATIBLE'
                print(reader, activity, status, 'observed_columns=', columns,
                      'observed_rows=', repr(rows), 'columns_match=', columns_ok,
                      'rows_match=', rows_ok, 'binary_types_match=', blobs_ok)
                assert rows_ok and blobs_ok
            except sqlite3.Error as error:
                status = 'SQL_ERROR'
                print(reader, activity, status, type(error).__name__ + ':', str(error))
                assert str(error) == 'no such column: title'
            assert status == expected_status[checkpoint][reader]
    assert db.execute(queries['OLD']).fetchall() == written
    print('\\nPASS: rollback preserves representative update, insert, untouched row and exact BLOB bytes.')
finally:
    db.close()
after = {str(p): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in paths}
assert before == after
assert paths == sorted(p for p in Path('.').iterdir() if p.is_file())
print('PASS: supplied file hashes unchanged; no scratch files created.')
PY"
